text:
Marathon Petroleum rose modestly today after a sharp week-long selloff. The stock's recovery is modest and coincides with stabilization in crude oil markets following the back-and-forth on U.S.-Iran tensions—crude fell nearly 8% last week on hopes of diplomatic progress, but today's news of Trump rejecting Iran's ceasefire offer and signaling renewed military action after midterms may have halted further weakness. US crude is holding near $96/barrel, and refineries are running at 94% capacity with healthy product inventories, supporting the company's refining margins.

The broader picture is one of volatility around geopolitical risk. The stock dropped over 8% from mid-September to just three days ago amid oil price swings tied to Iran-U.S. rhetoric, and today's slight recovery reflects the market's uncertainty—investors are still pricing in conflicting signals of escalation versus diplomacy, which naturally limits any sustained price movement in either direction.
